clue.text: Athletic activity photographed, playing on green

parts.note: a photograph is a shot, so photographed means shot
on a golf green the play is putting

explanation.surface: A sporting pastime is captured on camera while someone plays golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing the heavy ball is a standard track-and-field event, an athletic pursuit.

clue.text: How wise the human race presumably is?

definitions.text: How wise the human race presumably is?

parts.words: How wise the human race presumably is?
parts.note: our species is Homo sapiens, the 'wise man', so the human race must be wise by name

explanation.definitionFit: The word means wise, and is the root of the Latin name given to modern humans.

clue.text: Some professor I elected to college

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A university academic is voted onto the staff of a college.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of an Oxford college, so it is an example of a college; the 'to' is the clue's link.

clue.text: As remover of nuisances, quiet deceit is cunningly used

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet

indicators.note: the words are worked craftily into a new order, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Quiet trickery is slyly employed to get rid of something annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is only a link; 'deceit' tempts as a definition of trickery, but the whole sense is the chemical that removes nuisances.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical that kills pests is something that removes troublesome nuisances from crops.

clue.text: In match, daughter united

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: In a marriage, a daughter is joined to her partner.
explanation.walkthrough: A TIE is a British term for a single game in a knockout competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotted together means joined, so the word is a synonym for united.

clue.text: Disrespectful lines not altered

indicators.note: altered says the letters of the preceding words are changed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some rude lines have been left unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not altered' reads as unchanged, but 'not' is fodder and 'altered' alone signals the rearrangement of LINES and NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rude and showing no respect is the core sense of this adjective.

clue.text: A politically incorrect soft toy? My word!

definitions.meaning: a black-faced rag doll once common in Britain, now seen as racist

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the dated name of a controversial rag doll and a mild exclamation of surprise.

clue.text: Tense, perhaps, after practice?

parts.note: practice makes ..., as the saying goes, and one grammatical tense bears the same name

explanation.definitionFit: It names a grammatical tense and is what the proverb says practice makes you.

clue.text: Ram held by means of big cages

indicators.note: held says the ram's word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Aries is the zodiac sign of the ram
via means by way of, by means of

explanation.surface: A male sheep is confined using large pens.
explanation.definitionFit: Large enclosures for keeping birds are big cages.

clue.text: Pagan woman looks inquisitively at girl

parts.note: to pry is to look nosily, so looks inquisitively means pries
Tess is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A heathen woman nosily stares at a young girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A female priest of a pagan religion is an example of a pagan woman.

clue.text: Bar one gets purchase from

definitions.meaning: purchase is mechanical grip or advantage, which this tool supplies

explanation.definitionFit: It is a bar, and the tool that gives purchase, or mechanical advantage, when shifting loads.

clue.text: The French admitted to returning rice cake

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside, so one piece goes into another
returning says the word rice is read backwards

parts.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: The French have taken to rice cakes coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rice cake' reads as one snack, but rice is fodder turned round and the cake is the definition, reaching back only to the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A long choux pastry filled with cream is a kind of cake.

clue.text: Have fun with valuable box, but be careful

parts.note: to play is to have fun
a safe is a box for valuables

explanation.surface: Enjoy yourself with a strongbox, but take care.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to avoid risks, which is to be careful.

clue.text: Northerner coming back in alarm

indicators.note: coming back says the word for the northerner is read backwards

parts.note: a Scot comes from the north of Britain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A northern visitor returns in a state of alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell rung as a warning signal is an alarm.

clue.text: Firm beginning to make simple object

parts.note: CO, company, is a firm

indicators.note: beginning to says take the first letter of the next word

parts.note: plain means simple

explanation.surface: A company starts to make a basic item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb, to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To object is to protest or grumble, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Child so, not spared rod? Perfect!

definitions.meaning: the proverb says spare the rod and spoil the child, so a child not spared it is not spoiled

explanation.definitionFit: It describes a child who has not been indulged, and anything untouched and flawless.

clue.text: Enter plea to restore leafy feature of London, say

indicators.note: to restore means put into a different, repaired state, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plea is lodged to bring back some greenery in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to restore' rearranges ENTER and PLEA. The 'London' kind is a hybrid tree that lines the city's streets.
explanation.definitionFit: A large leafy tree is a typical feature of London streets, the London variety being famous.

clue.text: Chuck Heather for being clumsy

parts.note: bung is British slang for chuck, to throw
ling is another name for heather

explanation.surface: Someone throws Heather out for being awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant. To BUNG is British slang for toss.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things awkwardly and ineptly is being clumsy.

clue.text: Leapt to one's feet, being arrogant

definitions.meaning: self-important, putting on airs above one's station

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the past tense of springing upright and an adjective for upstart arrogance.

clue.text: Sailor's working for US president

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and the 's gives the S
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A seaman's job is for the American president.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Jackson was the seventh president of the United States.

clue.text: Emperor a usurper, do we hear?

indicators.note: do we hear signals that the word is spoken and sounds like another

parts.note: a usurper seizes power, so is a seizer

explanation.surface: Was an emperor a usurper, we wonder?
explanation.definitionFit: The title was borne by Roman emperors and became a word for emperor.

clue.text: Decide to tackle puzzle a second time

definitions.meaning: to make up one's mind firmly

definitions.text: to tackle puzzle a second time
definitions.meaning: ..., to work out the puzzle again

explanation.definitionFit: It means to make a firm decision, and split as re-solve to work something out again.

clue.text: Shout and gesture that identifies one to audience

parts.note: to call is to shout
a sign is a gesture

explanation.surface: A cry and a wave let the crowd know who you are.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters and radio operators use this code to identify themselves to listeners.

clue.text: Absolute female monarch

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch

explanation.surface: A woman ruler with total power.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter or complete, as in sheer nonsense, is absolute.

clue.text: Ambassador has caviare for superstars

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
caviare is fish roe, so roes

explanation.surface: A diplomat serves fish eggs to celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolised figures, such as sporting greats, are superstars.

clue.text: In debt, making nothing on the side

parts.note: O, zero, is nothing
a wing is a side, as of a building or team

explanation.surface: Someone owes money while earning nothing on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Money still to be paid is owing, so one is in debt.

clue.text: Run into agent that's unusually active

indicators.note: into puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A secret agent runs in, remarkably energetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively and nimble, especially for one's age, is unusually active.

clue.text: Bad shot? Should be piece of cake

definitions.meaning: in golf or tennis a mis-hit that curves off line
a portion cut from a cake

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a mis-hit shot in golf and a wedge cut from a cake.

clue.text: I'm at only some of fair

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
partial means only some, not complete

explanation.surface: I am attending just part of the fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbiased and even-handed is the sense of fair here.

clue.text: School competition for sport

parts.note: Rugby is a famous English public school
a league is a sporting competition

explanation.surface: A school contest for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: RUGBY is an English public school, where the game was supposedly invented.
explanation.definitionFit: The thirteen-a-side code of rugby is a sport.
